title: What rhizoid needs to carry a mailing-list fork: non-GitHub tracking, a topic series per item, mail send-back, retire on landed, a distro package pin
waits: its owner's look-around (a backlog item in git-rhizoid.github.io, beside send-back-writes-the-upstream-item and cutting-as-cargo-dependency)
note: From linux-phone-oco: sxmo-utils (sr.ht, mailed) and the kernel (b4, mailed). (1) a cutting of a non-GitHub upstream: tracking by git fetch + push, created by gh repo create + push; (2) one topic branch per upstream item off tracking, rebased only before a send, and an integration branch merging the topics, never rebased, that consumers pin - the patch branch cut per item; (3) send-back by mail: format-patch/b4 prep of tracking..topic with cover letter and recipients, never sending, returned for the follower's upstream item; (4) retire a topic when upstream carries it (patch-id against tracking) and say so (landed, carried-in none); (5) a pin where a distro package reads it (APKBUILD source tag + sha512sums), the cargo item generalised. Meanwhile: plain git by decision 2026-11-18-upstream-forks and tad q carried.

title: update-pins moves a base's pin only when a file of the source's list changed between the pin and the latest release
note: docs releases several times a day; most releases do not touch the device layer and should open nothing in four bases. git diff --quiet vOLD vNEW -- the listed files (and the marked parts).

title: own is a named override with a status: an own file that differs from the source at the pin passes only while an upstream item of the base names it or the pin says own_why; an own tables.toml keeps the marked part
applied_upstream: idealkb v0.19.0 (decision 2026-11-18-own-says-why; [why] in the pin file, bin/check-own.sh)
note: Measured: docs' 6 own statements differ, decision.sql lacks --supersedes/--amends/--scope/--tracked-by since 0.14.0, no item names them; each device base's own tables.toml lacks 101 lines of 0.16.0's part (the known gap tables-own-drift). Yocto Upstream-Status and DEP-3 Forwarded, failing rather than warning (9.4% forwarded where it only warns). graph-drift.sh own-behind and own-part are the test.

title: When a base changed a followed file, update-pins also opens that change as a PR on the source at the pinned release and records an upstream item in the base
note: Not run live yet: no base differs (idealkb backlog exit3-sends-up-live).

title: rhizoid's scope: the follow tool for every edge a repository has (slice, tool pin, cutting), one status over all, both ways; status first, then follow by conformance with idealkb's follow.sh, send-back, cuttings
note: From research base-graph-measured and base-graph-world: no Rust or shell tool carries root-level files down and changes up (only copybara, JVM); the cutting case has no tool here. Build order, each replacing shell only once it passes the shell's tests: status (passes graph-drift.sh), follow (passes idealkb bin/test-follow.sh fixtures byte for byte; keeps the pin naming its source, one owner per file, the followers' gate), send-back (idealkb-exit3-sends-up's shape), cuttings (rhizoid-carries-mail-forks). Never a template engine, a merge of data or rows. Its base's items slice-consumption, followers-one-pin-bump, send-back-writes-the-upstream-item and implement-cli are reshaped to it.

title: scripts/workarounds: read backlog items across bases, sites only, and say each workaround's way out - so a lane rule and a script read the same
note: From decision 2026-11-18-workarounds-read-as-one (linux-phone-oco/docs). Measured on 2026-11-18 over surya-lab, google-walleye-lab and docs at origin/main: every marker found is a record's note or AGENTS.md's 'WORKAROUND(item-id)' example, so the reader reports 'due: item-id' on two bases; a marker naming a backlog item (our own work, here a kept kernel) reads 'not known' and so 'due'; the lines give a state but not the way out. Asked: --base repeatable; ITEM looked up in upstream_items then backlog; skip data/, rendered docs/, research/ and the example; print SITE: ITEM - STATE - way out (patch to UPSTREAM | carried in FORK, due once the device runs it | our work, backlog ITEM in BASE | due: retire). The check that shows it: research/workarounds/2026-11-18/workarounds-read.sh in linux-phone-oco/docs (B, C, D). The skill text (look-around-first, after a fix) may say a lane rule is a workaround too, marked where the lane reads it.
